title: Downtime minimization — Ops playpad & release annotator (Feb 2025)
content:
Goal: minimize user-visible downtime during model/infra changes by tightening preflight, making a fast rollback path, and annotating release notes live for customer comms. This doc is a compact ops playpad + release notes draft that the launch conductor can carry in-pocket during a push.

High level constraints / assumptions:
- Target: < 60s user-visible interruption for hosted API (95th percentile) for this push.
- Deploys happen 02/22/2025 02:00–06:00 UTC (low traffic window).
- Primary path uses blue/green with traffic ramp; secondary path is immediate rollback to previous model shard.
- Dedicated capacity customers unaffected (config pinned) unless we flip global router.

Quick preflight checklist (T-72h, T-24h, T-1h):
- T-72h: finish smoke test matrix; owners assigned (see Open items). Jira ENG-2314 must be green.
- T-48h: tag release image, upload artifact to artifact-repo, create annotated release notes draft and share with PM.
- T-24h: telemetry baseline capture (latency, error-rate, token-cost per request) for both primary region and DR region.
- T-6h: notify SRE on-call, set increased sampling (1%) for traces and 100% for canary cohort.
- T-1h: confirm rollback runbook exists in incident channel, ensure feature-flag kill-switch is tested.

Hour-by-hour rollout calendar (simplified):
- 02:00 UTC: cut canary with 0.5% traffic, run canary smoke tests (latency tail, 5 sample prompts, KV-cache integrity).
- 02:12 UTC: if smoke OK, escalate to 5% for 10m (telemetry: sampling + per-route error trend + cost delta).
- 02:30 UTC: 25% for 20m (let autoscaler settle; watch cold-start error spikes).
- 03:00 UTC: 75% for 10m (validate throughput P95 and throughput per GPU).
- 03:20 UTC: 100% ramp if no signals. Hold 30m at 100% to watch customer-facing logs.
- 03:50–04:10 UTC: post-roll checks and begin deprecation of old pool (graceful drain).

Abort/rollback triggers (automated + human):
- Automated: sustained increase in 5xx rate > 0.5% absolute, latency P95 > baseline + 200ms for 3 consecutive 1m buckets, or token-cost jump > 30% on route x100.
- Human: SEV or cross-team paging to #deploys from SRE or serving-runtime lead.
- If triggered: immediate traffic-shift back to previous version + start incident template (section at bottom).

Fast rollback steps (cheat sequence for on-call):
1) Set traffic routing to previous model variant (use router CLI: router shift --from=<new> --to=<prev> --instant).
2) Post status in #deploys with rollback tag and reason.
3) Kick rollback-validation smoke tests; confirm success within 3m.
4) Open postmortem stub in Confluence and add initial notes.

Smoke tests (must be automated in pipeline):
- Basic: /health, /v1/generate (3 short prompts), embedding sanity on 5 sample docs.
- KV cache: warm with long-context prompts and validate repeated prefix responses.
- Consistency: deterministic prompt with seed should match known output hash (for deterministic models).
- Billing/measure: ensure token accounting matches preflight snapshot within tolerance.

Telemetry & observability to monitor (live dashboard tile list):
- Global: 5xx rate, 4xx rate, client error uptick, P50/P95 latency, tail-latency heatmap.
- Model-specific: avg tokens per request, cost-per-token estimate, KV cache hit ratio, memory pressure on GPUs.
- Other: queue depth, autoscaler event counts, routing errors per region.

Release notes (customer-facing draft — short):
Title: "February 2025 inference improvements — reduced latency and safer rollouts"
Body: "Today we rolled out an update to our inference routing and model serving that reduces cold-start latency and improves stability. We’ve added an improved rollback path and finer-grained traffic ramping to reduce customer impact during future releases. No action required from customers. If you manage pinned model versions on Dedicated/Private, your configuration is unchanged. See the detailed engineer notes for changelog and telemetry.
Known impacts: none observed during the canary period. If you see anomalies, contact support@redwood.ai with request-id from your client logs."

Internal release notes (engineer-oriented):
- Artifact: release-image:2025-02-22-rls-07
- Primary change: router sidecar backoff tuning; kernel selection tweak for chunked-attention; faster cache warm paths.
- PRs: #421 (router ramping), #429 (kernel tweak), #432 (cache warm).

Open items (owners):
- Add end-to-end billing smoke to CI (Priya Nair) — due 2025-02-15.
- Finalize user-facing wording and legal review (Marco Diaz + Legal) — due 2025-02-17.
- Confirm DR region capacity and cross-region failover TTL (Ethan Brooks) — due 2025-02-18.

Communication plan (who to ping and when):
- T-24h: email to cs-ops and account managers with impacted customers list (PM to prepare).
- Launch: post short status in #deploys every major step (canary, ramp, full). Use "Deploy:Downtime-Min" tag.
- Post-roll: 1hr after 100% hold, publish internal annotated release notes to Confluence and copy to shared drive.

Incident template (initial messages to paste):
Subject: [Rollback] Feb22 Downtime-Min Release — <short reason>
Body: "We observed X (metric), shifting traffic to previous variant. Current status: rolling back. On-call: <name>. ETA for resolution: 20m. Owners: SRE (Ethan), Serving (Priya), Router (Marco)."

Notes to conductor / small practical tips:
- Keep a terminal with router CLI and telemetry dashboard open; pre-warm auth tokens.
- If traffic-shift fails, escalate to network infra and consider region-level drain (last resort).
- Avoid simultaneous infra changes (no infra patches + this release).

Appendix: quick commands
- router shift --from=release-image:2025-02-22-rls-07 --to=release-image:2025-02-15-stable --instant
- smoke-ci run --suite=release-minimal --timeout=300s

Draft changelog note (append to GitHub release):
- "Tuned router ramping policy to reduce tail-latency during model swaps; improved kernel selector for chunked attention; faster KV cache warm path. No customer-facing API changes."

Questions / unresolved:
- Do we want to add a brief rollback audit entry to billing when rollback occurs? (cost implications) — action: Marco to propose.
- Should we make canary cohort 1% persistent for 15m by default for future low-risk deploys? (ops preference) — discuss in next release retro.

If anything is unclear or you want a condensed one-page cheat card for on-call, ping me (Ava).
